Ordinary ties mean nobody rules. Eyrie rule a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or stop someone else ruling.

answer.ruling: Compare each player’s total warriors plus buildings in the clearing; a player rules only when their total is greater than every other player’s total.

source_passages.quotation: **Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.** Resolve these six steps:

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle
source_passages.quotation: 1. **Ambush:** Defender may play one ambush matching clearing (birds are wild). Attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. Defender's card is discarded; a foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise defender immediately deals two hits, then discards ambush. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Ambush hits are not limited by defending warriors.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle
source_passages.quotation: 3. **Roll:** Higher die is attacker's rolled hits, lower defender's; equal dice give equal results. Each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defending reverses the dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle
source_passages.quotation: 5. **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra hit for **defenseless**; Vagabond is instead defenseless if it has no undamaged swords.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle
source_passages.quotation: 6. **Deal hits:** Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but **all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens**. It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces' removal. Both sides deal their counted hits; losing warriors does not retroactively change the rolled cap. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores **one VP each**, even while defending and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.

answer.ruling: To initiate battle, choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy defender; you need not rule it. The defender may play one matching ambush (birds are wild). The attacker may foil with a matching ambush; the defender’s card is discarded and a foiled ambush causes no hits. Otherwise the defender immediately deals two hits and discards the ambush. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain after those hits, battle ends immediately; ambush hits are not capped by defending warriors.

When Alliance defends, it reverses the dice assignment. Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors for its rolled-hit limit.

answer.ruling: Add extra hits without a warrior cap, then subtract ignored hits. If the defender has no warriors, the attacker gets one defenseless hit; Vagabond is defenseless instead when it has no undamaged swords.

source_passages.quotation: **Craft (4.1):** **Every crafting piece gets its suit from the clearing containing it.** The card's **bottom-left crafting icons** require pieces of those clearing suits; the card's own suit does not define the cost. Craft a card from hand when your faction permits.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Craft
source_passages.quotation: - **Marquise, Eyrie and Alliance cost:** For **each icon**, activate **one workshop, roost or sympathy in a clearing matching that icon's suit**, respectively. A crafting piece gets its suit from its clearing. Combine eligible pieces as needed, but **each piece may activate only once per turn**.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Craft
source_passages.quotation: - Immediate effect (paper box): resolve, then discard the **crafting card**. An item card requires the corresponding **item token** in the map supply, or it cannot be crafted. Take the item token into Crafted Items and score the VP printed on the card, subject to Eyrie exception. The item token stays; the crafting card is discarded. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle — Craft
source_passages.quotation: - Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to the personal duplicate check above. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

source_passages.quotation: **Personal duplicate check:** Only an identical persistent effect **in your own play area** prevents you from crafting that effect again. Other players' copies do not count for this duplicate restriction.

answer.ruling: Craft a card from hand when permitted by your faction, paying its bottom-left icons with crafting pieces whose clearing suits match each icon; the card’s own suit does not set the cost. Marquise activates workshops, Eyrie roosts, and Alliance sympathy, one eligible piece per icon.

source_passages.quotation: **Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.ruling: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP.

At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse, rabbit, or fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of the matching suit. Bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting a condition before that timing does not immediately win.
An activated dominance card cannot be removed or replaced.

source_passages.quotation: **Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.ruling: If a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as an available dominance card instead.
During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. This is separate from activating dominance and requires no faction action allowance.
An available bird dominance card remains bird, so only a bird hand card can pay to take it; a bird hand card may pay to take a non-bird dominance card.

7. Set up factions in their letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.

source_passages.section: Marquise de Cat — Keep and Field Hospitals
source_passages.quotation: **Keep:** Only Marquise may **place** pieces in its clearing; other players may **move** pieces into it. The keep cannot be placed again if removed. **Field Hospitals:** Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the keep clearing instead of supply. This can apply outside battle. Without a keep there is no destination for hospitals. See **FAQ & Rulings** for Hospitals during an ambush at the Keep.

source_passages.section: FAQ & Rulings — Field Hospitals during an ambush at the Keep
source_passages.quotation: - **Field Hospitals during an ambush at the Keep:** Marquise may spend a matching card immediately when its warriors are removed, returning them to the Keep clearing **before** checking whether the ambush left no attacking warriors or pawns. If returned warriors remain there, battle continues. Without Hospitals, battle ends if no attackers remain after the ambush. (FAQ under 4.3.1 and 6.2.3.)

answer.ruling: Only the Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. If the Keep is removed, it cannot be placed again.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat — Keep and Field Hospitals

answer.ruling: Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, the Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of returning them to supply. This also applies outside battle, and without a Keep there is no destination for the Hospitals. During an ambush at the Keep, pay immediately when warriors are removed and return them before checking whether the attacker has any warriors or pawns left; if returned warriors remain, battle continues.

source_passages.quotation: **Daylight:** First craft with workshops. Then take **up to three actions**, plus **one per bird card spent outside an action**, in any order and number except Recruit's limit:
- **March:** Up to two moves; either may use the same or different warriors. Do not interrupt the compound action to spend a bird card or take another action.
- **Recruit:** One warrior at **each recruiter**; only **once per turn**. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.
- **Overwork:** Spend a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

answer.ruling: First craft with workshops. Then take up to three actions, plus one action per bird card spent outside an action; take actions in any order and number subject to Recruit’s once-per-turn limit.
A March is up to two moves, using the same or different warriors. It is one compound action: do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action.
Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and may be taken only once per turn. If supply cannot fill every recruiter, place the maximum available and choose among eligible recruiters.
Overwork costs one card matching the sawmill’s clearing and places one wood there.

source_passages.quotation: - **Build:** Choose a clearing you rule with open slot and choose building type. Take the leftmost building of that type. Pay cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place building; score VP on uncovered space. You cannot build without full wood cost, the building and legal slot.

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing you rule that has an open building slot, then choose a building type.

Pay the cost shown atop the selected building’s column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other clearings you rule that are connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. A full wood payment is required.
Take the leftmost building of the chosen type, place it in the legal slot, and score the VP shown on the newly uncovered track space. Building also requires that the building piece be available.

source_passages.quotation:
**Birdsong, in order:**

1. **Emergency Orders:** If hand empty, draw one.
2. **Add to Decree:** Must add one or two hand cards, **at most one added bird card**. Each goes to any column; columns have no size limit.
3. **A New Roost:** If no roosts on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors **where all these pieces can be placed**.

answer.ruling: At the start of Birdsong, if the Eyrie hand is empty, draw one card.
Add one or two cards from hand to any Decree columns, with at most one of the added cards being a bird card. There is no column size limit.
If there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors among clearings where all of those pieces can be placed.

source_passages.quotation: **Daylight — resolve the Decree:** Craft using roosts first, then resolve **every Decree card**, column by column **Recruit → Move → Battle → Build**. Within one column choose card order freely. Bird is wild. **If any required action cannot be fully completed, immediately enter Turmoil: you cannot skip the card or continue other columns.** For a prompted placement with too few pieces, first place the maximum possible, then enter Turmoil because the action remains incomplete (publisher clarification in **FAQ & Rulings**). Each card requires:

| Decree column | Match the card's suit to | Required procedure for one card |
|---|---|---|
| Recruit | Clearing with a roost | Place **one warrior at one chosen roost** there; Charismatic must instead place **two warriors** there |
| Move | Origin clearing | Move **at least one warrior**, obeying ordinary path and rule requirements |
| Battle | Clearing of battle | Initiate a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy |
| Build | Target clearing | Place one roost in a clearing you rule, with an open slot and **no roost already there** |
**Bird Decree cards are wild in every column:** choose any clearing suit, while still meeting that action’s other requirements.

answer.ruling: First craft using roosts. Then resolve every Decree card in column order Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; choose card order freely within a column. Bird cards are wild. If any required action cannot be completed fully, enter Turmoil immediately; you may neither skip that card nor continue to later columns.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Daylight — resolve the Decree

answer.ruling: Recruit cards match a clearing with a roost and place one warrior at one chosen roost (Charismatic places two). Move cards match the origin and require moving at least one warrior under ordinary path and rule requirements. Battle cards match the battle clearing and initiate a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build cards match the target and place one roost in a clearing the Eyrie rule, with an open slot and no roost already there. A bird Decree card may choose any clearing suit, while still meeting the action’s other requirements.

evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Daylight — resolve the Decree; Decree procedure

source_passages.quotation: **Turmoil, in order:** Lose one VP per bird Decree card **including both Loyal Viziers**; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement. If none face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing. Retuck Viziers in new leader's columns. End Daylight and proceed to the full normal Evening: **score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, then discard to five**. **Turmoil does not remove your map warriors or buildings.**

answer.ruling: Lose one VP for each bird Decree card, counting both Loyal Viziers. Discard every Decree card except the Viziers.
Flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement. If none are face up, flip all leaders face up before choosing. Retuck both Viziers in the new leader’s columns.

answer.part: Map pieces and rest of turn
answer.ruling: Turmoil ends Daylight, leaves Eyrie warriors and buildings on the map, and proceeds to the normal Evening: score the VP shown on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard down to five.

source_passages.quotation: **Outrage:** Each time another player **removes sympathy** or **moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing**, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters. Moving a group costs one card per affected move, rather than one per warrior. If no matching cards including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. **If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; payment or the no-match draw still occurs.** Merely battling there is no trigger unless sympathy is removed; placing warriors there and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.ruling: Another player triggers Outrage by removing sympathy or moving any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. Merely battling in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger it unless sympathy is removed. Placing warriors there and moving only the Vagabond pawn do not trigger it.

answer.part: Payment for affected movement or removal
answer.ruling: The affected player adds one hand card matching the clearing’s suit to Supporters, with birds counting as matches. Moving a group costs one matching card per affected move, not per warrior.

answer.part: No matching hand card and full Supporters
answer.ruling: If the player has no matching card, including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, discard the incoming Outrage card; the required payment or no-match draw still occurs.

source_passages.quotation: **Birdsong:** Both Revolt and Spread Sympathy take place **during Birdsong**. Complete **all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy**; each may be performed any number of times. **For both actions, every supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild.** Once spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt this Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt:

- **Revolt:** Choose sympathetic clearing without a base, matching a base still on your board. Spend **two matching supporters**. **Remove all enemy pieces there, scoring one normal removal VP per enemy building/token removed**; then place matching base. Place warriors there equal to number of sympathetic clearings matching the base's printed suit (including revolt clearing), and one warrior in Officers box. Resolve the effect even if a prompted placement cannot be completed: place the maximum possible, without adding a base-placement prerequisite. Enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed.

- **Spread Sympathy:** Choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy; if no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend matching supporters shown above next sympathy token. **Martial Law:** add one matching supporter if chosen clearing has at least three warriors of **one other player**. Place token and score uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing. Keep's placement ban still applies.

answer.ruling: Both actions occur during Birdsong, and each may be performed any number of times. Complete all Revolts before beginning any Spread Sympathy. Once spreading begins, no further Revolt may be taken that Birdsong, so newly placed sympathy cannot fund a same-Birdsong Revolt. Every supporter spent for either action must match its target clearing; birds are wild.

Choose a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on the Alliance board, and spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces there, scoring one ordinary removal VP per enemy building or token removed, then place the matching base. Place warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base’s printed suit, including the revolt clearing, and place one warrior in Officers. For incomplete prompted placements, place the maximum possible; no additional base-placement prerequisite is added. An enemy Vagabond is not removed and instead damages three items.

answer.part: Spread Sympathy eligibility, cost, and results
answer.ruling: Choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy; if there is no sympathy anywhere, choose any clearing. Spend the number of matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token. Martial Law adds one matching supporter if the chosen clearing has at least three warriors belonging to one other player. Place the sympathy token and score the uncovered track VP. Only one sympathy token may occupy a clearing, and the Keep’s placement ban still applies.

evidence: Woodland Alliance — Birdsong; Revolt; Spread Sympathy

source_passages.quotation: - **Train during Daylight:** Spend a **hand card** matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers box. Supporters cannot pay Train. Each officer allows one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.
| Organize | Remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing; place sympathy there; score the uncovered VP |

Organize spends no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost; it still needs legal token placement. **After operations**, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard hand down to five.

**Losing a base:** Discard all supporters matching its clearing **including birds**, remove half officers **rounded up**. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five. Do this whenever a base is removed.

answer.ruling: During Daylight, spend a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one warrior from supply in the Officers box. Supporters cannot pay for Train.

For one Organize operation, remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score the uncovered VP. It costs no supporters and has no sympathy-adjacency requirement or Martial Law cost, but legal token placement is still required.
Each officer permits one Evening military operation; taking operations does not consume officers.
When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, and remove half the officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five.

evidence: Woodland Alliance — Daylight; Evening; Losing a base

source_passages.quotation: 1. **Refresh:** First count tea **already face up on Refresh track**; flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then three more exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh this step. Refreshing changes face, not damaged status.

2. **Slip (optional):** Move to an adjacent clearing or forest, exhausting **no boots**, even into hostile warriors. Ignore all effects preventing movement **out of** a clearing. **Forest adjacency for Slip:** a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do.

- **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.
1. If in forest, **Rest**: return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. This does not refresh undamaged exhausted items.
2. **Always draw**, even after forest Rest: one card plus one per face-up coins on track.

answer.ruling: At Birdsong, count tea already face up on the Refresh track. Flip two exhausted items face up per counted tea, then flip three additional exhausted items. Tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh during that step; refreshing changes face, not damaged status.

Slip is optional: move to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignore effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. A forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by one printed path; on Winter the river also divides forests as paths do.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Birdsong (Slip); Actions — Shared movement (forest adjacency)

answer.ruling: For normal Daylight Move, exhaust one boot, plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (including for forced moves). Ignore rule. This action cannot enter a forest; from a forest, move only to an adjacent clearing.

If in a forest at Evening, return all damaged items to Satchel and flip them face up; ready tea, coins, and bags move to tracks if possible. Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coin on the track, even after Rest.

evidence: Vagabond — Birdsong; Daylight; Evening; Actions — Shared movement

source_passages.quotation: - **Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin's clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

- **Quest (matching clearing only):** Choose a face-up quest matching clearing; exhaust its **two listed items**, put quest in play area completed. Choose either VP equal to matching completed quests **including this one**, or draw two cards. Draw replacement quest into public display. No cards are spent to pay a quest.
- **Repair:** Exhaust hammer; move one damaged item to Satchel **keeping current face**. Ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

answer.ruling: In the ruin’s clearing, exhaust a torch to take one hidden item face up into Satchel or its track. Score one VP if an item is taken. Remove the ruin and free its building slot when its last item is taken.

In a clearing matching the quest, choose a face-up quest and exhaust its two listed items; put it in the play area as completed. Choose either VP equal to the number of matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards. Draw a replacement quest into the public display. No cards are spent to pay for the quest.
Exhaust a hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel, keeping its current face. Ready tea, coins, or bags move to their tracks if space is available.

source_passages.quotation: - **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.

- **Strike:** Exhaust crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another of its faction pieces instead. Check hostility. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
- Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item. Coalition with Hostile faction resets its marker to Indifferent.

answer.ruling: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves that faction’s relationship marker to Hostile, except when the allied-battle-loss rule applies.

During battle on the Vagabond’s own turn, score one extra VP per Hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile. A Hostile building or token removed in such a battle normally gives two VP total: one ordinary removal VP plus one Infamy; an eligible Hostile warrior gives one Infamy, with the initial Hostile-causing warrior excluded from Infamy. Infamy does not score on another player’s turn or from Strike.
Aid cannot move a faction’s marker out of Hostile, though Aid can still obtain a crafted item. Coalition with a Hostile faction resets its marker to Indifferent.
answer.evidence: Vagabond — Relationships (Aid and Hostile); Scoring / Victory Conditions — Vagabond coalition

answer.ruling: Exhaust a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing. Only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another piece of its faction instead. Check hostility; Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). **An already-activated dominance player cannot be chosen:** they have no score marker on the track (publisher clarification in **FAQ & Rulings**). Compare eligible players still on the score track. Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner later activates and wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.ruling: With four or more players, during the Vagabond’s own Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate dominance to form a coalition with another player not already in a coalition. A player who already activated dominance cannot be chosen because they have no score marker on the track.
Choose the player whose VP is lowest among players other than the Vagabond; choose among ties. Compare eligible players still on the score track.

Place the Vagabond’s score marker on the partner’s faction board and stop scoring VP. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including if the partner later activates and wins by dominance. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not make the partner an enemy or grant Allied relationship powers.

source_passages.quotation: - **Precedence:** Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, faction rule wins. **Cannot is absolute** unless explicitly overridden. (1.1.)

answer.ruling: Cards override the Law, and the Law overrides Learning to Play. Apply general and faction rules together when possible; if incompatible, the faction rule wins.
“Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden. An ordinary card can override a cannot only when it explicitly does so; otherwise the prohibition remains.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects with the same timing, the attacker chooses their order.
A Marquise March’s two moves form one compound action; do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action.

source_passages.quotation: Take turns clockwise: **Birdsong → Daylight → Evening**. “At start” effects precede all other phase effects; “at end” effects follow everything else in that phase, before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions. An action, ability or persistent effect cannot be interrupted unless an effect explicitly permits it; a Marquise March's two moves are one compound action. If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. (1.1.3, 1.4, 4.3.)

answer.ruling: “At start” effects happen before all other effects in the phase. “At end” effects happen after everything else in that phase and before the next phase.

answer.part: Beginning the last step of a turn
answer.ruling: Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except actions explicitly permitted at the end of Evening or the turn.

source_passages.section: Special Rules & Edge Cases — hand/deck information and agreements
source_passages.quotation: - Hand size is public, contents private: reveal/show only if explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed; actions require no consent. (1.2–3.)

answer.ruling: Hand size is public but hand contents are private; reveal or show the hand only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched or inspected; the deck may not.

answer.ruling: Agreements are non-binding. Cards may be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.

source_passages.quotation: - **Cards:** Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, even for multiple same-suit payments. **If prompted to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, you must treat your birds as that suit**; the instruction determines how many cards to give or discard. **Only a bird card can pay an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit and mouse cards cannot pay it.** Draw from shared deck top; when deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into new deck. (2.1.)

answer.ruling: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck.

Bird cards substitute for any non-bird suit, including for multiple payments of the same suit. When instructed to give or discard cards of a non-bird suit, treat birds as that suit; the instruction determines how many cards are given or discarded.
Only a bird card pays an explicit bird-card requirement; fox, rabbit, and mouse cards cannot pay it.
